meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'boy', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мальчики, тихо, он же совсем пьян!
examples.trans: Boys, easy, he is completely drunk!

examples.text: Как тебя зовут, мальчик?
examples.trans: What's your name, boy?

examples.text: Это мой мальчик.
examples.trans: This is my boy.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'quietly'.

examples.text: Мальчики, тихо, он же совсем пьян!
examples.trans: Boys, easy, he is completely drunk!

examples.text: Тише, дети спят!
examples.trans: Quiet, the children are asleep!

examples.text: Здесь тихо.
examples.trans: It's quiet here.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Он совсем один.
examples.trans: He's completely alone.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'drunk', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Он пьяный и хочет за руль сесть.
examples.trans: He is drunk and wants to get behind the wheel.

examples.text: И мы были пьяные.
examples.trans: And we were drunk.

examples.text: Он пришёл домой пьяный.
examples.trans: He came home drunk.
